newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says Kinshasa foreigners safe, staying.
newsitem.headline: France says Kinshasa foreigners safe, staying.

text.p: France said foreign nationals in Kinshasa were not being endangered during the rebel takeover of Kinshasa on Saturday and there were no immediate plans to evacuate them.
"At the moment, the security of the French community and other foreign nationals is not being threatened. No decision to evacuate them has been made so far," a foreign ministry spokesman said.
French radio and television reports from Congo's capital Brazzaville had said earlier that an evacuation was imminent.
French, U.S., British, Belgian and Portuguese troops are on standby in Brazzaville, across the Zaire river, to evacuate foreign nationals from Kinshasa if need be.

"We are monitoring the situation in Kinshasa with the utmost attention and our ambassador is in close touch with his colleagues from the countries concerned for a possible evacuation," the ministry spokesman said.
Six French patrol boats left Brazzaville for Kinshasa earlier on Saturday and French military officials said they would reinforce the ambassador's residence there.
